content:
A Middle Tennessee paranormal investigation team performed a paranormal investigation at Hendersonville’s historic Bradford-Berry House over the weekend.

Elite Vixen Paranormal is an all-women paranormal team founded in 2018 by Chinelle Gwartney and Sammantha Biggs. The team is based in Nashville, currently made up of seven members. Over the years, Elite Vixen Paranormal has built a reputation as a team.

“We’ve had many opportunities to investigate in many locations,” Gwartney said. “We are often called to assist with public investigations, multiple collaborations. We’ve done well to build our reputation and be a credible team.”

Over the weekend, Elite Vixen Paranormal visited the Bradford-Berry House for the first time for an investigation. While Gwartney was unable to attend the investigation, three other members of the team attended and the investigation was done outside of the historic home, as the house itself was not safe to enter.

“Each investigation is different,” Gwartney said. “Even if we’ve gone to the exact same location 37 times, every single investigation is going to be different.”

Gwartney first learned about the Bradford-Berry House over a year ago when a story about the home ran on a local news channel. She made a note of the location to follow up on it. Then, another member of Elite Vixen Paranormal, Jen Reed, came to Gwartney after hearing about the house from her father, Ron Zellem, who has since become a member of the Bradford-Berry Preservation Society.

“That’s one of the things that we do as investigators,” Gwartney said. “The money that we put into locations and the money that we bring into locations does nothing but preserve history. That’s kind of how we got involved with it, Ron was like, ‘This thing’s going on,’ and we can help to preserve this location.”

Gwartney defined an intelligent spirit as one that maintains its consciousness as a spirit. A residual spirit, Gwartney said, is one that does not retain its consciousness and one that is stuck in a time loop, where it repeats the same actions over and over again. Gwartney said that if a spirit interacts with equipment that makes light or sounds, those are intelligent spirits.

“We don’t go into locations claiming that they’re haunted,” Gwartney said. “We don’t go in trying to prove that they’re haunted. We do things from a more empirical, scientific standard where not everything is paranormal.”

Gwartney said that the team defaults to trying to explain things that happen on investigations through something naturally occurring or through scientific reasoning. After an investigation, the team shares what they found with colleagues and posts on social media to get the opinion of the masses.

“That way, we get all the different perspectives, including the skeptics,” Gwartney said. “I myself am a skeptical believer. What that means is I know that there’s paranormal activity that happens. I know that spiritual hauntings happen, but also I don’t believe that everything is paranormal.”

Saturday night’s investigation began at 7 p.m., running until just after 10 p.m. It began with donning headlamps, the team gathering at the back driveway to state their purpose and good intentions in coming to the property aloud. The team placed trace tape on the stride porch, which tracks movement through LED lights and began to work with dowsing rods, an Ovilus and other equipment surrounding a stone to the side of the Bradford Berry House.

Dowsing rods are handheld, L-shaped tools that investigators use to ask “yes” or “no” questions and to ask questions about directions. Throughout the night, one member of the Elite Vixen Paranormal team carried a pair of dowsing rods, asking questions and watching as the rods moved to answer. Nearby water can possibly interfere with dowsing rods.

Some responses were also recorded on an Ovilus, which is a device meant to translate EVPs into writing. Words that appeared on the Ovilus’s screen included the word “year” and others. The team also captured other possible interactions through a spirit box app that said “What happened?” and “Desolate.”

Other areas of investigation included a set of steps, the graveyard and other areas of the grounds.

“The very first thing about investigating with us – and actually on any investigation – is to have fun, because the more fun that you have on an investigation, the more fun the spirits are going to have, especially those that are considered intelligent spirits,” Gwartney said.
